Participants.
Participants in Experiments 4 and 5 were re-
cruited to complete a group performance study through Amazon
Mechanical Turk and were compensated $1.00 for their time. For
Experiment 4 (N  262), data from nine participants (3.45%) were
excluded prior to conducting analyses because of voicing suspi-
cion about their group existing. Of the remaining 253 participants
for Experiment 4, whose age ranged from 18 to 68 (Mage  32.9
years), 168 were women and 78 were men (7 did not disclose their
gender). For Experiment 5 (N  380) data from 12 participants
(3.16%) were omitted prior to conducting analyses because of
voicing suspicion about their group existing. Of the remaining 368
participants, whose age ranged from 18 to 66 (Mage  32.0), 231
were women and 128 were men (9 did not disclose their gender).

Originality
Table 3 presents the results obtained for the originality of leadership plans in the analysis of covariance. Openness proved to be a
signiﬁcant (F(1, 325) = 6.29, p ≤.01) covariate with openness proving to be positively related to the production of more original
plans. This ﬁnding, of course, is not surprising. A more critical ﬁnding emerged with respect to the main effect produced by the schema
manipulation. The schema manipulation yielded a signiﬁcant (F(1, 325) = 4.96, p ≤.05) main effect. Examination of the cell means
indicated that more original plans were obtained when few (M = 3.15, SE = .082) as opposed to many (M = 2.90, SE = .082)
schema were presented, providing support for Hypothesis 2 with regard to plan originality. Apparently, leaders ﬁnd it more difﬁcult
to produce original plans when they are asked to work with a large number of concepts.
Elegance
Table 4 presents the results obtained in the analysis of covariance connected for plan elegance. Intelligence (F(1, 319) = 5.28,
p ≤.05) and need for cognition (F(1, 319) = 7.09, p ≤.01) both proved to be signiﬁcant covariates, and, as might be expected,
both intelligence and need for cognition were positively related to the production of more elegant leadership plans. Leader style
also proved to be signiﬁcant (F(1, 319) = 4.54, p ≤.05) covariate. It was found that more elegant plans tended to be produced by peo-
ple evidencing a charismatic leadership style.
